Cloudflare\'s free WARP network as a real WireGuard config: run the open-source wgcf tool once on a PC to register and export an unlimited free profile.
Create a free account, then dashboard → Downloads → WireGuard configuration. The free plan generates configs for the free servers; paid plans unlock all locations.

Swedish privacy provider (diskless servers). After login, generate WireGuard keys and server configs from the account area.
Login → generate WireGuard keys, choose the server and download the .conf. Their guides page covers every platform.
Client Area → Config Generator → select WireGuard as protocol and a server, then generate the .conf.
Direct generator link: log in and the member-zone WireGuard tool builds a config for any server and port.
The WireGuard configurator sits in the members area — pick a server, download the profile.
Account portal → WireGuard under Service Management → choose a location and press Generate to download the config.
User page → VPN → Manual setup → Router → WireGuard. Create the key and copy the generated config into a .conf file.

NordLynx (WireGuard) is built into the official apps, while the account panel only exports OpenVPN configs.
No official WireGuard .conf export — community tools use your account token; the generator-friendly providers above are the easy path

One-command installer that turns a Raspberry Pi (or any Debian/Ubuntu box) into a WireGuard server with per-device profiles.

WireGuard-based mesh for your own devices, free for personal use — its apps manage keys for you; pair with Headscale above for raw .conf control.
Open-source WireGuard management platform (free cloud plan or fully self-hosted) — groups, ACLs and DNS over your own mesh.
Self-hosted WireGuard network manager: a central dashboard spins up peers and hands you standard client configs for any device.
Open-source, WireGuard-based VPN / zero-trust gateway — self-host on a small VPS and download a per-user profile.

Travel routers with WireGuard built in: the admin panel\'s VPN page generates server configs and client profiles (with QR) in two clicks — verified.
Turn almost any router into a WireGuard server or client: install the luci-proto-wireguard package and add the interface from LuCI.
pfSense and OPNsense firewalls ship WireGuard — create a server and peers in the web UI, then export peer configs for your devices.
RouterOS 7 has native WireGuard — create the interface, add peers and print the client config from the terminal.

RiseupVPN is the donation-funded, no-account VPN from the Riseup collective — its gateways speak WireGuard, and the linked community configurator exports ready-to-import .conf files for every gateway.
The official RiseupVPN client doesn\'t export .conf files — the linked open-source tool signs you in and builds the configs against Riseup\'s own gateways
Long-running free VPN service: pick one of the public US / UK / Canada / Germany / France servers and download a ready WireGuard .conf or QR code — no account, no signup, funded by ads and donations.
Configs expire after 7 days and the shared page password rotates periodically — re-download to refresh
Verified: the member area\'s Manual Configuration page issues WireGuard profiles — add the free WireGuard add-on, pick a location and download the .conf.
WireGuard configs arrive as a member-area add-on — enable it once under Subscriptions
Feature-packed admin portal for your own WireGuard server: web UI with QR codes, LDAP/OAuth users and one-click wg-quick .conf downloads — a single Go binary, Docker-ready.
A private network system that uses WireGuard under the hood: invite-token peers, CIDR-based organisation and NAT traversal for your own overlay mesh.
Self-hosted WireGuard platform with true MFA on every connection, SSO/LDAP identity integration and client profiles users download themselves — open-source core.
The respected custom ASUS firmware — its VPN Director imports provider WireGuard profiles, so one .conf tunnels the whole household.
WireGuard needs a Wi-Fi 6/7 ASUS model (386.5+ firmware) — older Wi-Fi 5 routers stay on OpenVPN
The veteran third-party router firmware: current builds ship a WireGuard tab for both server and client — turn spare hardware into a tunnel endpoint.
Debian-based router/firewall OS: WireGuard interfaces are first-class with official site-to-site and road-warrior recipes in the docs.
Small privacy-focused Dutch provider: log in, open the WireGuard page and download a ZIP of ready-made configs for every location — with router bundles for GL.iNet and Merlin.
The privacy-first registrar collective runs a lean VPN: add a VPN slot, press “Use WireGuard” and download the .conf — crypto payments welcome.
One active client config at a time — re-download it (or add another slot) when you switch devices
Veteran token-based privacy service: paste your access token into the WireGuard page and it generates the config — Simple mode mints keys for you, Advanced keeps your private key on-device.
Open-source self-hosted VPN that installs WireGuard (or the block-resistant AmneziaWG fork) on your own VPS in a few clicks — and exports plain .conf files for SecureNet.
Management layer over an existing WireGuard network: a web console with monitoring, peer expiry alerts and QR codes, synced by a lightweight agent on each host.

The LinuxServer.io Docker image: one compose file builds a full WireGuard server with a web UI for peers, QR codes and client configs — plus client-mode tunnels that route the container itself through a provider.
docker-compose stack bundling WireGuard, Pi-hole and Unbound: a full- or split-tunnel VPN with ad blocking and recursive DNS in one deployment, managed from a web UI.
Open-source distributed VPN server with WireGuard mode on every connection — replicated servers, static client IPs, client-to-client routing and ~13s failover, managed from a polished web console.
WireGuard mode rides on the Pritunl client\'s multi-layer authentication — connections are not vanilla wg-quick .conf imports
UniFi gateways (Dream Machine, Cloud Gateway and friends) ship a WireGuard server and client inside the Network app — create users and download per-device profiles.
The Broadcom-router firmware with a full WireGuard GUI: import a wg-quick provider .conf, set policy routing and a kill switch — verified against the official wiki.
WireGuard GUI ships on ARM builds only — MIPS models lack it; provider .conf import since r2025.3
The open-source firewall platform with WireGuard built in: the VPN → WireGuard page for tunnels and peers, with official recipes for remote-access and site-to-site setups.
The community firewall distribution with native WireGuard support: host-to-net roadwarrior and net-to-net tunnels configured straight from the web GUI.
ASUS stock firmware gained a WireGuard server and client under VPN Fusion — generate profiles with QR codes right from the router\'s web GUI, no third-party firmware needed.
Needs firmware 3.0.0.4.388 or later on VPN Fusion-supported models — check the model list linked in the guide
Third-party Windows client around WireGuard with a modern UI, kill switch, split tunneling and high throughput — a popular alternative to the official app.
Free for personal / educational / non-profit use — not the official WireGuard client
WireGuard is built into NetworkManager on every modern desktop Linux: create the interface with nmcli or the connection editor — Red Hat\'s official RHEL 9 guide covers server and client end to end.
The official WireGuard app — useful to verify a profile, or to scan a provider QR and re-export the .conf for SecureNet.
The same official client from F-Droid, without Google services.
Official clients for Windows, macOS, Linux and more — the .conf files work identically in SecureNet.
The official iOS client — open any .conf from Files, scan a provider\'s QR, or verify a profile before importing into SecureNet.
The official Mac client from the App Store — the same .conf files work identically in SecureNet on Android.

string-array.name: guide_steps_free
string-array.item: Pick a free source: Proton (sign-up → Downloads → WireGuard) or Cloudflare WARP via the wgcf tool.
Generate and download the .conf — no payment needed.
Prefer your own server? A permanent free VPS tier (Oracle Cloud Always Free) + wg-easy from the self-hosted section costs nothing.
Import into SecureNet: Servers → Import → file, QR or paste.

string-array.name: guide_steps_paid
string-array.item: Pick a provider with a config generator — every provider marked above.
Subscribe; most offer a 30-day money-back guarantee, so testing is risk-free.
In the dashboard open the WireGuard config generator, choose server and port, download the .conf.
Import into SecureNet and connect — keep the provider\'s file as a backup.

string-array.name: guide_steps_selfhosted
string-array.item: Get any small VPS (Oracle Cloud has a permanent free tier; Hetzner or DigitalOcean ~ $4/month).
Run one installer: wg-easy (Docker), PiVPN, Algo or the wireguard-install script.
Open UDP 51820 in the provider\'s firewall and download a .conf per device.
Import each profile into SecureNet — your own server, zero monthly fees.

string-array.name: guide_steps_routers
string-array.item: Open your router\'s admin panel (GL.iNet: VPN → WireGuard; OpenWrt: install luci-proto-wireguard).
Create a WireGuard server or client interface.
Add a client peer and export its .conf (or scan the QR code shown).
Import the profile into SecureNet so your phone carries the same tunnel anywhere.

string-array.name: guide_steps_apps
string-array.item: Install the official WireGuard client for your platform.
Import the provider\'s .conf or scan their QR inside the app.
Verify the handshake works outside SecureNet.
Re-import the same .conf into SecureNet for the full feature set: split tunneling, kill switch, multi-hop.

string-array.name: guide_tips
string-array.item: Treat a .conf like a password: it holds keys that identify your device — never share or post it.
Beware of random \"free WireGuard config\" lists on social media — whoever built the config can see and route your traffic.
No handshake? Re-check the endpoint port (try 51820, then 443) and confirm the server public key matches the provider\'s page.
Connected but no internet? The provider\'s DNS is usually missing — set DNS = 1.1.1.1 in the config.
Slow or unstable on mobile data? Lower MTU to 1280–1380; the optimizer screen can suggest a value.
One profile per device keeps keys unique — and a PresharedKey (when offered) adds another strong layer.
